$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-2x(t)-5y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=5x(t)-2y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above. The eigenvalues of the system's matrix are ${\lambda }_{1,2}=-2\pm 5\text{i},$ for which the corresponding eigenvectors are ${v}_{1,2}=[\pm \text{i},1]^{T},$ respectively. Select the correct options in the reasoning below.The general solution of the system is

$$
[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]={c}_{1}{e}^{-2t}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}{e}^{-2t}[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

For example, when ${c}_{1}=1$ and ${c}_{2}=0,$ we obtain the following curve:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x={{field-1}} \\ y={{field-2}}\end{aligned}
$$

examples.knowledge_point: Sketching the Phase Portrait of a System
examples.problem:
Consider the system of linear differential equations below.

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=9x(t)\end{aligned}
$$

The eigenvalues of the system's matrix are $\lambda_{1,2} = \pm3\text{i},$ for which the corresponding eigenvectors are $\mathbf{v}_{1,2} = [\pm \text{i}, 3]^T,$ respectively. Given that the general solution of the system is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069757/assets/6feea8db62000e44334251a96c39bd8d0d8d7b1ec9a61380f3a5b4b613ea6c80.png)
sketch the phase portrait of the system of differential equations given above.
examples.worked_solution:
We are given that the general solution of the system is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069757/assets/bceb494a6baeca8695157b4fd285b2880a242367747c0d72a0f573612ef87652.png)

For example, when $c_1=1$ and $c_2=0,$ we obtain the following curve:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) \\ y=3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the coordinates (rounded to two decimal places) of several points on the curve, we get the table below.

| $t$ | $0$ | $\dfrac{\pi}{12}$ | $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $0$ | $-0.71$ | $-1$ |
| $y$ | $3$ | $2.12$ | $0$ |

Let's sketch this solution in the phase space.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069757/assets/3c2ea4467854f749e07f5ae3922273a2ebd441da4fb9df834ce0676157e856a2.png)

Notice that $|\sin(3t)| \leq 1$ and $|\cos(3t)| \leq 1.$ Thus, the obtained curve is bounded. So, we have an ellipse that is traversed counterclockwise.

The phase portrait of our system looks as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069757/assets/df8e7ae5f7ff7281cbdbf5849dc94faf59d2421621dc5009b21eeb947485d153.png)
